newsitem.title: JAPAN: Venezuela, Japan fail to solve Venalum veto dispute.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela, Japan fail to solve Venalum veto dispute.

text.p: Officials from the Venezuelan government and a Japanese aluminium consortium have still not reached an agreement in talks to end their dispute over the Venalum smelter, said Alberto Poletto president of the Venezuela Investment Fund (FIV).
"Still now we don't have an agreement," he said. "I'm still optimistic." he added in a telphone interview with Reuters.
He said the Venezuelan delegation would meet early on Thursday to evaluate the results of the negotiations up to now.
"They're willing to accept some changes. It depends on some compromise on our side." Poletto said.

However, he and Elias Ynaty, president of Coporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG), the other top official in the delegation, would not meet again with the Japanese before leaving on Thursday for South Korea.
He said a technical team would stay in Japan through Friday.
Poletto said the technical team would then return to Venezuela and that further talks may be held with Japanese at a later date in Venezuela.

The Venezuelan government, which owns 80 percent of Venalum and hopes to privatise it later this year, has been in a bitter dispute since the beginning of 1996 with the Japanese, who hold a 20 percent share of the facility, regarding Japanese veto powers over Venalum decisions.
Venezuela attempted to pressure the Japanese consortium into giving up its veto power by suspending in February their 90,000 tonnes a year equity shipments of ingot.

Poletto added that the privatisation of Venalum would proceed even if the Japanese do not relinquish their veto powers, although he said the price received for the sale of Venalum shares would be lower if the Japanese veto power were to be maintained.
"With the veto power or without the veto power, our decision is to privatise," he said "We are willing to give concessions," he added
He also stated that Venezuela had no intention of expropriating the Japanese holdings.
